decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Jeffrey M. Lacker.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace in recent …”

changes.quote: Household spending has advanced a bit more quickly, but growth in business fixed investment has slowed.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has continued to advance, but growth in business fixed investment appears to have slowed.”

changes.quote: Inflation recently picked up somewhat, reflecting higher energy prices.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Inflation has been subdued, although the prices of some key commodities have increased recently.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that, without sufficient policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee is concerned that, without further policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor mar…”

changes.quote: To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee will continue purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee agreed…”

tone_quotes.quote: In particular, the Committee also decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate are likely to be warranted at least through mid-2015.
Furthermore, strains in global financial markets continue to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.

These actions, which together will increase the Committee’s holdings of longer-term securities by about $85 billion each month through the end of the year, should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.06% APR costs about $50.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.8% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.39% would rise by about $1.66 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.8%, and employers added an average of 168k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (September 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 74%, cut 26%, hike 1%.
